body.statement: For any finite collection of EasyRCA lag-specific transmission queries on one fixed coordinate set and alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), rank only queries for which the certified partial \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\).  Under the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:cylinder\text{-}hac}\), if their population scores are separated by a fixed positive margin, the plug-in ranking is consistent.  A \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) output carries its directly constructed fixed-alphabet lag-switch certificate, and an \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) output records an unresolved query; both are excluded rather than assigned a causal score.
body.justification: The consumer contract now separates causal scores, certified nonidentification, and unresolved abstention.
body.gap: Unknown queries cannot yet be ranked causally.
body.consumer: Operators see why each excluded lag is failed or unresolved.
body.proof_tex: For every successful query, \(\mathrm{thm:tid\text{-}dichotomy}\) proves that the returned cylinder functional equals the causal target throughout the compatible class.  Applying \(\mathrm{prop:finite\text{-}margin\text{-}plugin\text{-}ranking}\) to the fixed finite collection of successful functionals shows that, under the stated sampling assumptions and positive population margin, their plug-in ordering is correct with probability tending to one.  The failure branch is sound by the same theorem and carries the explicit lag-switch pair; the unknown branch makes no causal assertion.  Excluding both tags from ranking therefore assigns scores only where a uniform identifying functional has been proved.
